data.cultural_impact: The name "Wafid" can be seen as symbolic of determination and persistence, as one who passes through things suggests overcoming obstacles and continuing on a path despite challenges. In an Islamic context, the name could also reflect a dedication to regular religious practices, such as daily prayers or recitation of the Quran.
data.spiritual_significance: In spiritual terms, the name "Wafid" could represent a person who is constant in their faith and devotion to God. This name encourages individuals to frequently engage in spiritual practices and to persist in their search for closeness to the divine, even when faced with difficulties or setbacks. The name's emphasis on continuous action aligns with Islamic teachings that encourage the regular performance of rituals and acts of worship. Ultimately, the name "Wafid" serves as a reminder to remain committed to one's beliefs and to trust in the unwavering presence of God throughout life's journey.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Khaldun's 'Muqaddimah' mentioned Wafid as a title of the Hafsid Emirs of Tunisia. The name Wafid carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun (1332-1404) was a renowned historian and sociologist. In his seminal work 'Muqaddimah', he documented the history and social sciences. He described the Hafsid Emirs of Tunisia as 'Wafid', referring to their transient or interim rule.

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi recorded that the Fatimid Caliph Al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah granted the title 'Wafid' to the governor of Egypt, Badr al-Jamali.
historical_references.context: Al-Maqrizi (1364-1442) was an Egyptian historian. In his work 'Ittiqad Ahl al-Qudat', he described that the Fatimid Caliph Al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah (r. 996-1021) bestowed the title 'Wafid' upon the powerful vizier Badr al-Jamali, implying a transient or temporary position of authority.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Wafid' in Islam is derived from a Hadith where Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) described a believer as someone who 'continuously seeks knowledge'. This name holds significance in today's world as a symbol of constant growth, learning, and improvement. On Instagram, Wafid is seen as a hashtag used by individuals sharing their spiritual journeys and daily inspirations. TikTok creators use the name for videos on personal development and mental health awareness tips. On YouTube, educational channels and motivational speakers use the name to brand their content, emphasizing the importance of continuous learning and improvement.

name_in_real_life.story: Aisha Wafid, a teacher in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, shares that their name Wafid meaning "Passing, Frequent, Continuous, Transient" has been a source of inspiration throughout their life, motivating them to be a positive influence in their community.
